Hi John — thanks for the details and the network diagram. Answers inline to help your change board review: 

1) GPU compatibility:
- Redwood runtime supports both H100-class and A100-class configurations. Performance/throughput will vary; we can provide performance profiles for your representative workload. Quantized models (8-bit/4-bit) reduce VRAM requirements and CPU overhead for preprocessing, but we still recommend at least 1.5–2x peak token‑throughput headroom in VRAM per GPU.

2) Power / cooling / RU:
- Typical 4x GPU 2U server: ~2x 30A single-phase circuits per rack (depending on PSU config). For DGX-style integrated enclosures, plan for 3‑phase 50A where available. Recommended: reserve 10–12U for initial cluster (control plane + 3x inference nodes + spare), scale rack count as needed.

3) Offline upgrade & signing:
- Process we recommend: 
  a) Redwood provides a signed release bundle (RSA-4096 signature) and SHA256 manifests.
  b) On your side, the offline verification utility (we provide a small binary) verifies the signature against your stored Redwood public key and validates manifest hashes.
  c) Apply in staging node first (air-gapped staging), run regression suite (we provide containerized tests), then promote to production nodes.
- HSM: not required to run Redwood, but customers can use an HSM/KMS for storing the private keys used in your internal signing workflow. Redwood will accept externally-signed bundles if you elect to verify with your keys.
- Rollback: We maintain previous image bundles for 30 days; rollback is a reverse bundle apply + cache invalidation step documented in the attached offline upgrade runbook.

4) Maintenance ops / change freeze:
- We will produce a 1-page change-summary and a non-disruptive patch timeline (target: 30–45 minutes for non-rolling config updates; 2–4 hours for full node image replacement if a full reboot is required). The actual window depends on your cluster size and whether you want canary promotions — we recommend 2 node staggered upgrades to avoid capacity loss.

Next steps we can take this week:
- I'll drop a draft offline upgrade runbook (redwood_onprem_upgrade_process.docx) and the signed-bundle verification utility.
- Marissa: please propose 2 workshop slots (60–90m) and include your procurement lead so we can discuss lead times.

Happy to jump on a call to walk the team through the runbook.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
